questions.text: National Grid & Power Dependency: Reliance on external power: (1) Grid reliability in operating areas; (2) Cost of diesel vs grid power; (3) Fuel supply chain resilience; (4) Impact of fuel price shocks; (5) Partnership with power utilities; (6) Renewable energy transition plan; (7) Backup redundancy.
questions.evidence_required: Power mix analysis, Fuel cost reports, Utility contracts
questions.africa_specific_notes: Telcos are often the largest diesel consumers in the country. Grid failure = Network failure (eventually).

questions.text: Fiber & Backhaul Ecosystem: Connectivity backbone: (1) Reliance on national fiber backbone (NOFBI etc.); (2) Redundancy of international cables (undersea); (3) Cross-border connectivity; (4) Fiber cut frequency (road works); (5) Last-mile fiber rollout challenges; (6) Microwave backhaul reliance; (7) Satellite backup.
questions.evidence_required: Fiber network map, Redundancy plan, Incident logs (fiber cuts)
questions.africa_specific_notes: Landlocked countries rely on neighbors for undersea cable access. Road construction is the #1 enemy of fiber.

questions.text: Spectrum Policy & Allocation: Access to airwaves: (1) Fairness of spectrum allocation; (2) Cost of spectrum (auction vs beauty contest); (3) 4G/5G roadmap clarity; (4) Spectrum trading/sharing rules; (5) TV White Space usage; (6) License duration; (7) Political interference in allocation.
questions.evidence_required: Spectrum license, Policy documents, Auction reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Spectrum is scarce and expensive. Delays in 4G/5G spectrum release hold back the digital economy.

questions.text: Taxation & Fiscal Policy: Cost of doing business: (1) Excise duty on airtime/data; (2) Mobile money transaction taxes; (3) Import duties on equipment; (4) Multiple taxation (national vs county/state); (5) Stability of tax regime; (6) Impact on affordability; (7) Industry advocacy effectiveness.
questions.evidence_required: Tax impact assessment, Lobbying papers, Tariff analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Governments view Telcos as 'cash cows'. High taxes (e.g., 20% excise) directly reduce affordability and inclusion.

questions.text: Fintech & Developer Ecosystem: Enabling innovation: (1) Open APIs for developers (Mobile Money); (2) Sandbox availability; (3) Developer support/community; (4) Revenue share models (VAS); (5) Investment in local startups; (6) Ease of integration; (7) Intellectual Property respect.
questions.evidence_required: API portal stats, Developer feedback, Partnership list
questions.africa_specific_notes: Telcos are the platform. If they block access (or copy ideas), the startup ecosystem dies. Open APIs drive innovation.

questions.text: Mobile Money Interoperability: Connecting the financial system: (1) P2P interoperability (send to other networks); (2) Merchant interoperability (Paybill); (3) Bank-to-Wallet integration; (4) Cross-border remittance support; (5) Cost of interoperability; (6) Settlement efficiency; (7) Regulatory mandate compliance.
questions.evidence_required: Interoperability stats, Settlement logs, User experience tests
questions.africa_specific_notes: Walled gardens are breaking down. Regulators pushing for full interoperability to boost financial inclusion.

questions.text: Community Relations & NIMBY: Social license to operate: (1) Tower siting consultation; (2) Radiation fear management (health concerns); (3) Land lease fairness; (4) Community benefits (CSR); (5) Conflict resolution; (6) Visual impact of towers; (7) Noise pollution (generators).
questions.evidence_required: Community meeting minutes, EIA reports, Lease agreements
questions.africa_specific_notes: Communities often block tower construction due to radiation myths or land disputes. Generator noise at night is a nuisance.

questions.text: Digital Literacy & Cultural Adoption: Readiness for digital: (1) Language barriers (English vs Local); (2) Cultural relevance of content; (3) Trust in digital finance; (4) Gender norms (women owning phones); (5) Age demographics (youth bulge); (6) Urban vs Rural divide; (7) Impact of social media.
questions.evidence_required: Market research, Adoption studies, User personas
questions.africa_specific_notes: Technology must fit the culture. Women often share phones or are discouraged from owning them. Trust is hard to win, easy to lose.

scoring_notes: Layer 6 (Ecosystem) for Telecom in SSA: Power and Fiber infrastructure are the physical constraints. Taxation and Spectrum policy are the regulatory constraints. The developer ecosystem is the growth engine.
